questions.question: After a continuous LP is solved with Simplex LP in Excel, a sensitivity report can be produced. Which information does this report summarize?
options: Only the optimal values of the decision variables and the optimal objective value
The sequence of corner points visited by Simplex LP before reaching the optimum
Shadow prices for each decision variable and the optimal value of every constraint
Variable and constraint values, reduced costs, shadow prices and allowable changes

questions.question: In the constraint section of an Excel sensitivity report for a solved LP, a constraint $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le b$ has a Final Value. What is this number?
options: The right-hand side $b$ that the constraint finally allows
The slack $b-\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ left over at the optimal solution
The shadow price of the constraint at the optimal solution
The value of $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ at the optimal solution

questions.question: An Excel sensitivity report lists a right-hand side of 50 with Allowable Increase 20. How should the entry 20 be read?
options: The right-hand side may rise up to a total of 20
The right-hand side may rise by up to 20% of 50
The right-hand side may rise by up to 20, to 70
The left-hand side may rise by up to 20, to 70

questions.question: An Excel sensitivity report gives an allowable increase and decrease for each objective coefficient and each right-hand side of a solved LP. For which kind of change are these ranges meant?
options: Simultaneous changes in all parameters within their ranges
A change in one parameter, with the plan held fixed
A change in one parameter, with all other data fixed
Changes in the constraint coefficients $a_{ij}$ only

questions.question: A planner has an Excel sensitivity report for a solved LP and asks how the optimal value responds to a small change in one right-hand side. What does the report allow?
options: Answering from the report, without re-solving, within the range
Nothing, until the LP is re-solved with the changed right-hand side
Answering from the report, for a change of any size
Answering from the report, but only for integer changes

questions.question: For the LP $\max 3x_1+5x_2$ s.t. (1) $x_1\le4$, (2) $2x_2\le12$, (3) $3x_1+2x_2\le18$, $\boldsymbol{x}\ge0$ (optimum $(2,6)$, value 36), the sensitivity report lists constraint Final Values 2, 12 and 18 against right-hand sides 4, 12 and 18. Which constraints are binding at the optimum?
options: Constraints (1), (2) and (3)
Constraint (1) only
Constraint (3) only
Constraints (2) and (3)

questions.question: A pipe plant's LP has a processing-time constraint with right-hand side 2,400. In the sensitivity report this constraint has Final Value 624. How much processing time is unused at the optimum?

In the sensitivity report for the LP $\max 3x_1+5x_2$ s.t. (1) $x_1\le4$, (2) $2x_2\le12$, (3) $3x_1+2x_2\le18$, $\boldsymbol{x}\ge0$ (optimum $(2,6)$, value 36), the objective coefficient 3 of $x_1$ has Allowable Increase 4.5 and Allowable Decrease 3. Over which interval may this coefficient vary on its own with the current solution staying optimal?

A pipe plant's sensitivity report gives Final Values 72 large pipes, 48 small pipes and 0 sheets, with optimal profit 816. A small pipe earns 5 and a sheet earns 4. What profit does one large pipe earn, to one decimal place?

In the sensitivity report for the LP $\max 3x_1+5x_2$ s.t. (1) $x_1\le4$, (2) $2x_2\le12$, (3) $3x_1+2x_2\le18$, $\boldsymbol{x}\ge0$ (optimum $(2,6)$, value 36), constraint (1), $x_1\le4$, has Allowable Increase 1E+30. How far may its right-hand side 4 rise with the reported shadow price still valid?
options: Up to 34, reading 1E+30 as an increase of 30
Not at all: 1E+30 flags that no range exists
Up to 6, adding the slack 2 to the right-hand side
Without limit: 1E+30 marks an unlimited increase

questions.question: In an Excel sensitivity report for a maximization LP, a constraint $\boldsymbol{a}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}\le b$ has a Final Value strictly below its right-hand side $b$. What does this mean?
options: The optimal plan violates the constraint by that amount
The constraint is binding at the optimal plan
The optimal plan leaves part of $b$ unused
Solver lowered $b$ to the Final Value

questions.question: A right-hand side in an Excel sensitivity report has shadow price 2 and Allowable Increase 10. (A shadow price is the value change per unit RHS increase, valid within the allowable changes.) The right-hand side is raised by 25. What can be concluded from the report alone?
options: The value rises 20 over the first 10 units; then re-solve.
The value rises by exactly $2\cdot25=50$, the full change.
The value stays as it is, since 25 exceeds the increase 10.
The LP becomes infeasible, since 25 exceeds the increase 10.

questions.question: A model is first solved as a continuous LP with Simplex LP, and its sensitivity report is saved. Integer restrictions are then added and the model is solved again. Which model does the saved report describe?
options: The continuous LP that Simplex LP solved
The integer model, as it was solved last
Both models, since they share their data
Neither, until the integer model is re-solved

questions.question: For the LP $\max 3x_1+5x_2$ s.t. (1) $x_1\le4$, (2) $2x_2\le12$, (3) $3x_1+2x_2\le18$, $\boldsymbol{x}\ge0$ (optimum $(2,6)$, value 36), constraint (2) has shadow price 1.5, right-hand side 12, Allowable Increase 6 and Allowable Decrease 6. (A shadow price is the value change per unit RHS increase, valid within the allowable changes.) What is the optimal value if this right-hand side becomes 16?

For the LP $\max 3x_1+5x_2$ s.t. (1) $x_1\le4$, (2) $2x_2\le12$, (3) $3x_1+2x_2\le18$, $\boldsymbol{x}\ge0$ (optimum $(2,6)$, value 36), the shadow prices of (1), (2), (3) are 0, 1.5, 1, and (3) has Allowable Increase 6. (A shadow price is the value change per unit RHS increase, valid within the allowable changes.) RHS (3) rises from 18 to 30. What optimal value does re-solving give?

For the LP $\max 3x_1+5x_2$ s.t. (1) $x_1\le4$, (2) $2x_2\le12$, (3) $3x_1+2x_2\le18$, $\boldsymbol{x}\ge0$ (optimum $(2,6)$, value 36), the coefficient 3 of $x_1$ has Allowable Increase 4.5. The profit per unit of $x_1$ rises from 3 to 5, everything else fixed. What are the optimal plan and value?
options: $(2,6)$ with value 36
$(2,6)$ with value 38
$(4,3)$ with value 35
$(2,6)$ with value 40

questions.question: In a solved LP, the sensitivity report gives each of two right-hand sides its own allowable increase and decrease. A planner changes both at once, each change lying within its own reported range. What does the report guarantee?
options: The two predicted value changes can simply be added.
Both rates stay valid, as each change is inside its range.
Nothing jointly: each range assumes all other data fixed.
The joint prediction holds when both changes have the same sign.

questions.question: A student types the coefficient 30 instead of 3 into one constraint cell of an Excel model, solves with Simplex LP, and creates the sensitivity report. What do the report's values, rates and ranges describe?
options: The intended LP, since Solver checks the constraint cells for typing slips
The LP as entered, with the coefficient 30 in place, not the intended one
The LP as entered for its values, but the intended LP for its ranges
The intended LP, once the ranges are reread for the true coefficient 3

questions.question: A pipe plant's optimal plan makes 72 large pipes, 48 small pipes and no sheets, with profit 816; its processing-time constraint has Final Value 624 and right-hand side 2,400. Processing capacity is cut to 700, all else fixed. What happens?
options: Profit falls in proportion, to $816\cdot\tfrac{700}{2400}=238$
Plan and profit 816 stay optimal: it needs only 624 of 700
The plan becomes infeasible, since 700 is below 2,400
The LP must be re-solved, since every capacity cut changes the plan

questions.question: For the LP $\max 3x_1+5x_2$ s.t. (1) $x_1\le4$, (2) $2x_2\le12$, (3) $3x_1+2x_2\le18$, $\boldsymbol{x}\ge0$ (optimum $(2,6)$, value 36), (2) and (3) have shadow prices 1.5 and 1, allowable changes 6 each way. (A shadow price is the value change per unit RHS increase, valid within the allowable changes.) RHS (2) goes from 12 to 18 and RHS (3) from 18 to 14 together. What is the new optimal value?
